subject: Re: Quick check — transient analytics hop, KMS escrow & subprocessor blackout window
messages:
From: Jay Patel <jay.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: lena.morris@acmehealth.com, security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Transient analytics hop — clarifying the operational window and keys

Dylan — thanks again for the call this morning. We have three narrow asks before our security committee signs the DPA addendum: 

1) Confirm there is a bounded window for any cross-region analytics processing — how long can data leave EU/APAC before being purged from the non-primary region?
2) We need to understand key handling if you do transient KMS wrapping/unwrapping — can Redwood escrow a short-lived key (24–72h) and provide attestation when it is destroyed?
3) Subprocessor activation blackout: during onboarding we require a 48h notice before a new subprocessor becomes active for our tenant. Is that operationally possible?

Attached: DPA draft (with our redlines). Can you also send a short runbook we can give to our infra team?

Thanks,
Jay
Director, Security Operations
Acme Health

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Jay Patel <jay.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient analytics hop — clarifying the operational window and keys

Jay — appreciate the concise list. Summarizing our position and next steps below so Acme Health's security committee has a single place to review: 

- Bounded transient processing window: Redwood supports configurable "transient analytics hops" that are tenant-scoped. Default max: 72 hours in the non-primary region before automatic purge, with operational logs showing scope and timestamp. We can tighten that to 24 hours if required for your workload.

- KMS escrow and attestation: We can provision a short-lived, tenant-scoped wrap key that resides in our HSM-backed KMS. A typical pattern we propose:
  * Key TTL: customer-selectable (24/48/72 hours).
  * Escrow policy: Redwood holds a single-use wrap key and records a signed attestation log entry when the key is destroyed. We can include the attestation as part of the audit bundle (signed by our KMS CA).
  * Recommendation: For PHI workflows, select 24h TTL and narrow the scope to analytics only.

- Subprocessor activation blackout: We can implement a tenant-level 48h notification before activation for new subprocessors. Operational caveats: onboarding pipelines for some infra providers may require a short warmup window; our ops team will provide a blackout checklist to guarantee no traffic touches a new subprocessor during the 48h period.

Next actions:
- I'll attach a runbook (ops checklist + purge verification steps) and draft redline language for the DPA to capture the TTL + attestation commitment.
- Marissa will follow up with an export of the current subprocessor roster and an ops timeline for activations.
- Karthik: can you confirm whether the 24h TTL plus HSM attestation meets our support SLAs and what telemetry we can include in the audit bundle?

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs: DPA_draft_AcmeHealth_20270312.pdf, transient-egress-runbook_v1.docx]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, Jay Patel <jay.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient analytics hop — clarifying the operational window and keys

Jay/Dylan — technical confirmation below: 

- Purge semantics: when data is routed for transient analytics processing to a non-primary region, we maintain an immutable event (routing start time, target region, request id). The data lifecycle engine runs a TTL-based purge job that deletes payloads and associated KV caches. Deletion is asynchronous but auditable; we provide a purge completion event that includes a content-hash and timestamp.

- KMS workflow: the tenant wrap key is generated per-activation in our KMS. When TTL expires we trigger a destruction flow that:
  1) revokes key material from live nodes,
  2) invokes HSM zeroize,
  3) produces a signed destruction attestation (KMS CA signature + HSM serial).
We can include the signed attestation in the monthly audit package or provide it on-demand post-destruction.

- Blackout implementation: our onboarding pipeline supports a "hold" flag that prevents DNS/service endpoints from routing to new subprocessors until an explicit release. The 48h notice will be enforced by our onboarding control plane; we will also provide a realtime activation window in the audit log.

I'll bundle the technical appendix into the runbook. If you want, we can schedule a short handoff call with your infra team to walk through the purge/verif steps (30 min).

-Karthik
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jay Patel <jay.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lena.morris@acmehealth.com, security@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: Transient analytics hop — clarifying the operational window and keys

Thanks — that addresses most items. A couple follow-ups from our side before we finalize redlines: 

- Attestation delivery SLA: we would like attestations delivered within 48 hours of key destruction (on-demand). Can you commit to that?
- Audit visibility: please include the purge completion event (content-hash, timestamp) in the per-tenant audit stream — ideally via a secure S3 push or signed log we can ingest.
- During the 48h subprocessor blackout, will there be any scheduled maintenance windows that could implicitly activate fallback subprocessors? Need clarity so our change control team can sign off.

If those are OK, we should be able to proceed to signature. I asked our procurement team to prepare a counter-signature DocuSign envelope once we lock language.

Jay

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Jay Patel <jay.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient analytics hop — clarifying the operational window and keys

Jay — quick operational commitments from Redwood: 

- Attestation SLA: Redwood agrees to provide the signed key destruction attestation within 48 hours of destruction. We will stream the attestation to Acme Health's secure audit endpoint (s3 presigned PUT or signed log bundle), whichever you prefer.

- Purge completion events: we will include the purge completion event (content-hash + UTC timestamp + request id) in the per-tenant audit feed. Delivery options: secure S3 push, signed webhook, or inclusion in the monthly audit package. We'll enable secure S3 push by default for Acme Health and pair it with HMAC-signed metadata.

- Blackout & maintenance: no automated fallbacks will be activated during the 48h subprocessor blackout unless explicitly requested by Acme (or if a critical incident requires emergency fallback). Any emergency activation will be logged and trigger immediate notification to Acme's security contacts. We will also add change-control webhooks to surface upcoming scheduled maintenances that could affect onboarding windows.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Marissa: send the fresh subprocessor_roster_20270312.csv and the final runbook (transient-egress-runbook_v1.docx) by EOD today.
- Dylan/Legal: I'll prepare the small DPA addendum language that encodes the TTL options + attestation SLA + blackout clause and share a DocuSign envelope link.

Thanks — looking forward to finishing this out.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
